completions.text:
High blood pressure, or hypertension, is a condition where the force of the blood against the artery walls is consistently too high. It is usually classified based on repeated measurements rather than a single high reading. When diagnosing hypertension, healthcare providers typically look for blood pressure readings that are high on multiple occasions.

A single high reading can be caused by many factors, such as stress, activity level, or even the environment. Therefore, a diagnosis of hypertension usually requires at least two or more elevated readings taken at different times to confirm that it is a persistent condition.
